title: Gigaflow: Pipeline-Aware Sub-Traversal Caching for Modern SmartNICs
problem: Virtual switch (vSwitch) offloading to SmartNICs suffers from high cache miss rates and poor scalability as the flow rule space grows, because existing solutions cannot efficiently store or traverse the large and complex flow rule tables that modern cloud tenants require. This leads to bottlenecks in packet processing throughput at the NIC level.
motivation: Modern public and edge clouds rely on high-performance end-host network stacks to support diverse tenant workloads (distributed training, fast inference), and vSwitch offloading to SmartNICs is a key scalability lever, but it is undermined by the inability to handle growing flow rule spaces.
method: Gigaflow breaks down packet processing into stages and caches the filtering results from each stage, rather than only caching the final result. When the SmartNIC processes new packets, it can reuse these cached intermediate results for stages that match, avoiding redundant searches through the flow rule tables. By knowing which intermediate results are safe to reuse, Gigaflow improves cache performance and maintains high throughput even when flow rule tables are very large.
key_novelty: Gigaflow caches intermediate filtering results from each pipeline stage instead of just the final lookup, allowing SmartNICs to reuse results across packets and handle very large flow tables efficiently.
contributions: Pipeline-aware decomposition of vSwitch processing into cacheable sub-traversal units
Sub-traversal caching mechanism that improves hit rates for large flow rule spaces on SmartNICs
Scalable flow rule matching solution that addresses growing flow table sizes in modern multi-tenant clouds
Evaluation demonstrating improved throughput and reduced miss rates compared to existing SmartNIC offload solutions
